acceptance: A claim helper exists: write the claim (startRun + task_started) and push; push success means the claim was won, push rejection means another worker won and this worker stands down before any builder dispatch
A test proves two workers racing the same task on a local fixture remote produce exactly one winner (the loser stands down with no builder dispatched and no duplicate state)
Single-worker behavior is preserved: one task per tick, claim-first dispatch
This change does not enable parallel execution; parallel execution stays off until a later directive authorizes it
Work lands on branch phase2/atomic-claim via PR; merge only by the orchestrator after verification
evidence: Builder commit aea79b2935f060ea6c275fd5d3a46371efca8331 pushed to origin/phase2/atomic-claim (remote SHA confirmed by orchestrator)

Orchestrator re-ran npm test in worktree: 55 total, 54 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (pre-existing root skip); claim test file run 2 extra times by orchestrator (4/4 each) — 24 two-worker race rounds total across builder + orchestrator runs, each exactly one winner, no flakiness

Race design verified in test code: beforePush barrier holds both workers until both passed ls-remote + committed locally, then releases both pushes simultaneously; asserts exactly one WON + one LOST, remote tip = winner SHA, fake dispatch only for winner, loser branch gone

Claim-Nonce trailer verified in claim.mjs: every claim commit unique, so two workers can never produce identical commits that a push would treat as up to date; no --force, --force-with-lease, or + refspec anywhere (grep); push failure with branch absent throws instead of misreporting LOST

Single-worker behavior preserved: no runner/cron change in this PR; runner wiring (cron step replacing manual startRun-push with claim.mjs) is deferred to the Phase 2 plan as follow-up; parallel execution stays OFF
PR https://github.com/garzonandres2004/genesis/pull/20 (phase2/atomic-claim -> main); GitHub-server race not tested (claim() re-checks the remote tip and does not rely on rejection message text)
objective: Close the duplicate-processing gap with an atomic task claim (or equivalent concurrency guard) so two workers attempting the same task cannot both succeed. A branch-state check alone is not atomic and must not be assumed to be.
title: Phase 2: Atomic task claim
